metadata.title: Revised demo script — Hyundai CRETA N Line (dm_201201c4), written against the human product-demo playbook
metadata.written_by: Claude, by hand — not generated by the pipeline. Every figure below cites a fact id from the demo's own registry (72 facts) and every picture is one of the 13 uploaded images. Nothing is invented.
inputs_used: docs playbook: human_product_demo_playbook_car_laptop_saas.json (GP01–GP12, car discovery order, three customer contexts, quality checklist)
data/demos/dm_201201c4/understanding.json (fact registry F001–F072, images im01–im13, unknowns U01–U25)
data/demos/dm_201201c4/plan.json and script.json (the current plan and script)
the 13:46 session transcript where you said: comfortable in the city, good on long drives
metadata.batch_rule: one batch = at most 38 spoken words (about 20 seconds in this persona's recorded voice at 1.9 words per second), then a pause point; est_seconds = words / 1.9

diagnosis.your_question: Is the problem the system prompt or the information available?
diagnosis.verdict: Mostly the prompt and the plan. The registry already holds everything a comfort-led, city-plus-long-drive demo needs for seats, climate, rear seat, sunroof, charging, cruise control, safety and warranty. It is genuinely missing five things a comfort buyer asks about (ride quality, cabin noise, boot space and ground clearance, fuel efficiency, how the DCT creeps in traffic), and the correct behaviour for those is to say so and route them to the test drive — which the current script never does for comfort.
information_available_for_a_comfort_led_: F029 leatherette seats with N logo; F028 black interior with red inserts; F031 scoop seats, ambient lighting, rear window sunshade
F056 60:40 split rear seat, 2-step recline, rear AC vents, rear armrest with cup holders, rear sunshade
F032/F033 rear and front wireless chargers; F057 cooled glovebox, smart key, rain-sensing wipers, tilt-and-telescopic steering
F038 Bose 8-speaker audio; F039/F040 twin 10.25-inch screens; F041 wireless Android Auto / CarPlay
F023 Smart Cruise Control with Stop & Go on the DCT (plain cruise control otherwise); F020 drive modes; F022 paddle shifters
F003 253 Nm from 1 500 r/min (the everyday-traffic argument); F001 1.5-litre turbo petrol; F008 6-speed manual or 7-speed DCT
F049 six airbags standard; F054 ISOFIX; F052 ESC, hill-start assist, auto hold, all-wheel disc brakes; F047/F048 SmartSense Level 2 list; F055 parking sensors, rear camera, surround view
F061/F062/F063 3-year unlimited-km warranty, 3-year roadside assistance, extended warranty up to 7 years
F012 2 610 mm wheelbase; F014/F015 McPherson strut front, torsion beam rear (suspension type, not tuning)
information_missing_that_a_comfort_buyer: ride quality: the brochure only offers marketing copy, F072 'finely tuned suspension… hug the road' — no measurement
cabin noise / refinement: nothing in the sources
boot litres, ground clearance, kerb weight: open question U03
fuel efficiency: open question U02 (the brochure states no figure)
DCT behaviour in bumper-to-bumper traffic: open question U20
crash-test rating: open questions U10 / U22
price, EMI, delivery time: U01 / U05 / U08 (dealer-only by design)

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: The first thing the customer hears after giving their context is a fixed opening built around 'N10 fit and manual-versus-DCT' plus a takeaway line with four specs (torque, six airbags, DCT-only list).
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.playbook_rule: GP03 overview before detail (20–30 s, no spec list) · GP04 three USPs · GP07 underlying need → restate the need and demonstrate the outcome first
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.where: plan.py PLAN_SYSTEM asks for a 'decision frame + takeaway'; author.py renders them as spec-dense lines; player.js always plays the opening before personalisation

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: No greeting that names the brand and product before the first question; the intake asks two things at once (name + what would have to improve).
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.playbook_rule: GP01 greet before you gather · GP02 one low-pressure context choice · GP08 one question at a time

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: Discovery order is engine → gearbox → safety → cabin → tech → styling → terms, i.e. performance first. The car order in the playbook is exterior/access → cabin comfort → practicality → driving → safety → ownership.
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.where: plan.py segment ordering (primary outcome chosen = torque)

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: The plan picked five USPs and the transmission choice as the decision; the customer who says 'comfort' gets a frame about gearboxes.
Spec-speak survives the 'everyday buyer' setting: 'r/min', 'newton metres', 'Level 2', 'Frame: what you are actually deciding'.
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.playbook_rule: GP09 speak like a person · GP10 translate specifications into experience
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.where: author.py JARGON list lacks r/min, Nm-as-words, 'Level 2'; segment titles are written for the planner, not the customer

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: Lines state a feature and stop; the 'what that means for you' step is often missing, and the check-in questions are sometimes stacked.
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.where: author.py AUTHOR_SYSTEM (SAY/SHOW/TRANSLATE/CONFIRM is asked for, but the word budget squeezes out TRANSLATE)

what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.problem: Comfort gaps are never declared: nothing tells the customer that ride quality, noise and boot space are not in the brochure and belong to the test drive.
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.playbook_rule: GP11 prove without overpromising · quality checklist 'the seller states what still needs to be verified'
what_the_prompt_and_plan_got_wrong.where: author.py: unknowns are used for Q&A declines but not surfaced in the pitch

what_you_actually_heard_at_13_46: you: comfortable in the city, good on long drives
'Lovely to meet you, Anand. Let me set up what we're deciding, then I'll show you the result first.'
fixed opening line 1: 'You're deciding two things today: does the N10 suit your driving, and manual or DCT?'
fixed opening line 2: 'My takeaway: full pull from fifteen hundred r/min, six airbags standard, but drive modes…' with the airbag cut-away picture (im01)
you stopped the demo; the comfort route the planner had chosen never played

revised_script.persona: Ananya, Hyundai showroom product specialist. Warm, short sentences, contractions, one question at a time.
revised_script.pictures: im09 front three-quarter parked · im03 seats · im13 cockpit · im06 sunroof overhead · im11 tunnel drive · im10 wet road · im04 DCT console · im05 manual knob · im07 paddle · im01 airbag cut-away · im12 low-angle parked

step_1_greeting.line: Hello, and thanks for your interest in the Hyundai CRETA N Line. I'm Ananya.

step_2_context_choice.line: Would you like to tell me quickly what you're buying it for, or shall we just get started?
step_2_context_choice.rule: GP02 · GP08 — exactly one question, easy to decline
step_2_context_choice.if_the_customer_gives_context: acknowledge in their own words (see routing.underlying_need.acknowledge) — then continue with step 3; do not play anything generic in between

step_3_quick_overview.line: This is Hyundai's sportier take on the CRETA, for someone who wants a compact SUV that's comfortable every day but still feels quick. Ventilated leatherette seats, dual-zone climate and a panoramic sunroof set the cabin up.
step_3_quick_overview.rule: GP03 overview template: who it's for, primary experience, capabilities

step_3_quick_overview.line: Under the bonnet, a one-point-five litre turbo petrol with its full pull from fifteen hundred r/min, so it moves off cleanly in traffic without you working the gears.
step_3_quick_overview.rule: GP03 performance promise · GP10 spec translated into experience

step_4_usp_map.line: The three things I'd pay attention to are the cabin comfort, the way it pulls in everyday traffic, and what's standard on safety and warranty. Let me take them in that order, unless you'd rather start somewhere else.
step_4_usp_map.rule: GP04 three USPs (experience · performance · confidence) · offers the customer the wheel

step_5_guided_discovery.notice: One thing you'll notice first is the stance: eighteen-inch diamond-cut alloys with red calipers, red inserts on the bumpers and sills, and a twin-tip exhaust.
step_5_guided_discovery.meaning: It reads as the sporty one in the car park without being loud about it.
step_5_guided_discovery.check: Does the look matter to you, or is it mostly about how it drives?
step_5_guided_discovery.honest_gap: ground clearance and kerb weight are not in the brochure (U03) — say so if asked

step_5_guided_discovery.notice: Now the part you'd live with daily. Ventilated front seats for Indian summers, dual-zone climate so both sides set their own temperature, and an eight-way electric driver's seat you set once, precisely.

step_5_guided_discovery.meaning: The practical difference is fewer small irritations on a hot, slow commute. In the back, the seat reclines in two steps, with its own vents and a sunshade.
step_5_guided_discovery.rule: GP06 meaning + one check question · GP08

step_5_guided_discovery.notice: For daily errands: sixty-forty split rear seats, wireless charging front and rear, cooled glovebox, and a voice-controlled panoramic sunroof. Boot litres aren't in this brochure, so that's one to check in person.
step_5_guided_discovery.check: Do you carry much luggage on the long trips?
step_5_guided_discovery.honest_gap: boot space U03 — declared in the line itself

step_5_guided_discovery.area: Driving experience — the engine in traffic
step_5_guided_discovery.notice: On the road: the turbo's full pull comes from fifteen hundred r/min, the band you're already in at city speeds, so a gap on the flyover means one squeeze rather than two downshifts.
step_5_guided_discovery.rule: GP10 translate the number into the moment it changes

step_5_guided_discovery.notice: You choose a six-speed manual or a seven-speed DCT. Four things come only with the DCT: drive modes, traction modes, paddle shifters, and Smart Cruise with Stop and Go for crawling traffic.
step_5_guided_discovery.check: Is your daily drive mostly stop-and-go, or open road?

step_5_guided_discovery.line: On ride comfort, the brochure only says the suspension is tuned to hug the road. That's marketing copy, not a measurement, so it's the thing I'd have you judge on a rough patch during the test drive.
step_5_guided_discovery.honest_gap: ride quality and cabin noise — no data; route to the test drive
step_5_guided_discovery.rule: GP11 verified vs marketing kept separate · quality checklist 'state what still needs to be verified'

step_5_guided_discovery.notice: Six airbags are standard, along with ISOFIX anchors, disc brakes on all four wheels, and stability control. SmartSense Level 2 adds collision warning, lane keeping and a blind-spot monitor. Assistance, not self-driving.
step_5_guided_discovery.check: Anything there you'd like me to slow down on?
step_5_guided_discovery.honest_gap: no crash-test star rating in the brochure (U10/U22) — say so if asked
step_5_guided_discovery.rule: GP05 order 5 · GP11 (the picture of deployed airbags belongs HERE, not in the opening)

step_5_guided_discovery.line: One variant, the N10, manual or DCT. Warranty is three years unlimited kilometres with three years roadside assistance, extendable to seven years on petrol, subject to the written terms. Price, finance and delivery I'll get from your dealer.
step_5_guided_discovery.honest_gap: price, EMI, delivery: U01 / U05 / U08 — dealer callback
step_5_guided_discovery.rule: GP05 order 6 · GP11 contractual claims named as such

step_6_fit_summary.template: Based on what you've told me, the strongest fit is {{fit}}, and the one thing we should still verify is {{uncertainty}}.
step_6_fit_summary.underlying_need_version: Based on what you've told me, the strongest fit is the cabin for your city days and the DCT's cruise control for the long ones. The one thing we can't settle here is ride comfort on your roads.

step_7_next_step.line: The best next step is a test drive on your own commute plus one rough stretch, with whoever usually sits in the back. Shall I book that with the dealer?
step_7_next_step.rule: GP12 next sensible action that resolves the biggest remaining uncertainty (ride comfort) · P10 advance

routing.rule: GP07: the overview (steps 3–4) stays the same for everyone; the FIRST detailed section changes with the customer's signal; the fixed opening never plays after a stated need

no_information.note: balanced first pass; the customer's reactions at each check pick the deeper path

specific_want_example_dct.clarify_first: Perfect, that gives me a clear place to start. Is the automatic mainly for easier city driving, or for relaxed highway runs?
specific_want_example_dct.rule: GP07 specific want → clarify what the feature must achieve, then demonstrate it first

underlying_need_your_case.customer_said: I'm looking for a car which is comfortable to drive in the city but good to take on long drives.

acknowledge.line: Got it, Anand: easy in city traffic, and genuinely comfortable when you take it out for a long drive. Let me show you the cabin first, then the drive, then what's standard.
acknowledge.rule: GP07 restate the need in the customer's words · GP04 map · plays IMMEDIATELY after the customer speaks, recorded or generated, never a generic intro

custom_batches_the_planner_should_write.line: For the long drives you mentioned, the DCT's Smart Cruise with Stop and Go holds your distance on the highway and even in slow traffic; on the manual you get plain cruise control.
custom_batches_the_planner_should_write.rule: P07 reuse the buyer's nouns · every figure cited

custom_batches_the_planner_should_write.line: For the city days: ventilated seats and dual-zone climate keep a slow, hot commute bearable, and the electric parking brake with auto hold means no creeping at long signals.

underlying_need_your_case.note: with pauses and the customer's answers this runs 4–5 minutes; to hold your 3-minute rule for a stated need, keep d1 and d3 as optional and let the check-in answers skip them

honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.ride quality / cabin noise: The brochure gives no measurement, only the line about suspension tuning. I'd judge it on the test drive on your own roads.
honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.boot space / ground clearance / kerb wei: Not in this brochure. I can have the dealer confirm the numbers, or you check them in person.
honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.fuel efficiency: The brochure states no figure. If that's your first criterion I'd pause here; the dealer can quote the certified number.
honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.DCT in bumper-to-bumper traffic: The brochure lists Stop and Go cruise on the DCT but says nothing about how the clutch behaves at crawling speeds. That's exactly what a test drive in your traffic answers.
honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.crash rating: No star rating is printed in this brochure; six airbags and the SmartSense list are what's stated.
honest_gaps_to_say_when_asked.price / EMI / delivery: Those I always get from your dealer. If you share your number, someone will call you.

changes_vs_current_script: Greeting names the brand and product; the context request is one question and can be declined.
A 34-second plain-language overview replaces the 'decision frame + spec takeaway' opening; three USPs instead of five.
Discovery follows the car order: exterior → cabin → practicality → driving → safety → ownership. Cabin comfort moves from 5th to 2nd.
Every batch has notice → meaning → one check question, and stays under 38 words.
The airbag picture appears only in the safety section, never in the opening.
Ride comfort, noise, boot space, fuel efficiency and price are declared as things the brochure cannot settle, and the next step is designed to settle the biggest one.
For a customer who states a need, the acknowledgement restates it in their words and the comfort section plays first; no generic intro in between.
No 'r/min' as a unit of measure in the everyday register except inside the one torque line; no 'newton metres', no 'Level 2' without the plain explanation.
if_you_want_this_to_become_the_default: plan prompt: ask for three USPs covering experience, performance and confidence, and for the car discovery order; decision frame written in the customer's nouns
author prompt: greeting + single-question context choice; overview template GP03; mandatory 'meaning' step; declare the top three unknowns inside the pitch
player: after a stated need play the acknowledgement, then go to the personalised route; the standard overview is at most two batches
jargon list: add r/min, Nm, 'Level 2', 'IDC' equivalents for cars
